title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down. It is a scratch computation that goes with the previous page, which lists structures attached to a conformal surface: compatible pairs of antiholomorphic involutions (real structures), compact tori in Aut^+(X), and so on. The case treated here is a complex torus.

(1) Notation. Let V ≅ C be the universal cover, Π ⊂ V a lattice, and E = V/Π. Let σ be an antiholomorphic involution, so σ acts R-linearly on V, preserves Π, and has eigenvectors u_+ (eigenvalue +1) and u_- (eigenvalue −1).

(2) Lattice types. The jottings 'u_+, ½(u_+ + u_-)' and '(x+½y)u_+ + ½y u_-' describe the two kinds of σ-stable lattice:
- the 'rectangular' lattice Z u_+ ⊕ Z u_-;
- the 'rhombic' lattice spanned by u_+ and ½(u_+ + u_-), whose general element is x u_+ + y·½(u_+ + u_-) = (x+½y)u_+ + ½y u_-.

(3) Cohomology. From the exact sequence of ⟨σ⟩-modules 0 → Π → V → E → 0, and the vanishing of H^i(Z/2, V) for i>0 (V is uniquely divisible), one gets
H^1(⟨σ⟩, E) ≅ H^2(⟨σ⟩, Π) ≅ Π^σ / (1+σ)Π.
This group classifies, up to conjugation by translations, the antiholomorphic involutions of the form t_a∘σ. Equivalently, it classifies the real structures on E as a curve that share the same linear part.
- Rectangular lattice: Π^σ = Z u_+ and (1+σ)Π = 2Z u_+, so the group is Z/2. There are two classes: σ itself, with two real ovals, and t_{u_-/2}∘σ, which has no fixed points.
- Rhombic lattice: (1+σ)(½(u_+ + u_-)) = u_+, so the group is 0. There is one class, with one real oval.

(4) Degenerate case. The line z ↦ exp 2πiz records the uniformization C/Z ≅ C^* (G_m), the analogous computation for the cylinder.

The purpose is to classify real structures on tori, case by case, as input for the classification on the previous page and for the hyperbolicity dichotomy on the next page (P^1, C, C^*, elliptic curves versus hyperbolic surfaces).
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The computation H^1(Z/2,E) ≅ H^2(Z/2,Π) ≅ Π^σ/(1+σ)Π is correct, since H^*(Z/2,V)=0 in positive degrees and H^2 of a cyclic group equals invariants modulo norms. The page is fragmentary: it gives no explicit statement of which real structures arise or how many fixed ovals each has.

ideas.what: Classification of real forms / antiholomorphic involutions of an elliptic curve via H^1(Z/2, E) ≅ Π^σ/(1+σ)Π, distinguishing rectangular from rhombic lattices
ideas.modern_name: Real elliptic curves; Galois cohomology H^1(Gal(C/R), E); classification of real structures on complex tori
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Weichold; Comessatti for real abelian varieties; modern treatment by Silhol, Gross–Harris)

ideas.what: Exponential uniformization C → C^*, z ↦ exp 2πiz

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine scratch computation of the classical classification of real structures on elliptic curves via group cohomology. It supports the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' notes but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The page is rotated 180°; read upright, the order is z ↦ exp 2πiz, then the cohomology line, then the exact sequence, then the lattice jottings.
'0 → Z → V → E → 0' should read '0 → Π → V → E → 0' (Π = lattice).
'H^1(Γ, E) ≃ H^2(Γ, Z) ≃ Z^g/(1-σ)(Z^g)' should read 'H^1(⟨σ⟩, E) ≃ H^2(⟨σ⟩, Π) ≃ Π^σ/(1+σ)(Π)'. This means invariants modulo norms, not Z^g and not (1−σ).
The overlined/bracketed expression '(x+½y)u_+ + ½y u_-' carries a small 'n' or '~' mark above; it is the general element of the rhombic lattice spanned by u_+ and ½(u_+ + u_-).
